gates.title: Classic-inspired VB.NET versus actual VB4

claim_checks.claim: The pictured IDE is Visual Basic 4.0 (not VB.NET, not a mockup).
claim_checks.evidence: HIST-02 claim-checks: host caption 'Microsoft Visual Basic 4.0 32 bit - Edit', title bar 'Loan - Microsoft Visual Basic [design]', sibling About capture 'Microsoft Visual Basic Version 4.0 / For 32-bit Windows Development'. This asset uses that file unchanged (SHA-256 re-checked by build.py and verify.py).

claim_checks.claim: UI panel names on screen match VB4 (R03 required handling).
claim_checks.evidence: label_checks above: Toolbox, Properties Window and Code Window are supported by VB 4.0-applicable Microsoft KB text and by the screenshot. Form Designer is VB6-documented descriptive wording for a visible form window. Project Explorer is VB6 terminology; VB4's Microsoft term is Project window (Q140350).

gates.reason: The picture is authentic VB4 and three of five labels are VB4-documented names. 'Project Explorer' (and, less critically, 'Form Designer') is later-version wording, and the narration's form/code-window description only partly matches this capture. Those are wording decisions for the Writing Lead that evidence cannot settle, so R03 stays blocked for release. No War/SCRIPT.md edit was made.

claim_checks.claim: The proof is kept out of cleared media.
claim_checks.evidence: state.json and delivery.json release_status 'blocked', unresolved_gates R03 and R14; no file placed in any cleared-media bin.

gates.reason: The underlying screenshot's rights are unresolved upstream, and whether callout marks over a whole Microsoft screenshot are permitted is an open legal/edit question. Internal proof only.

review_questions.question: Microsoft's screenshot terms say 'Do not alter the screenshot except to resize it' and 'Do not use portions of screenshots'. five-callouts keeps the whole screenshot but draws 5 px outlines on five window frames and five leader lines over empty desktop (every covered original pixel is listed in evidence/placement-checks.json; no code or text is covered). Are callout marks over a whole Microsoft screenshot acceptable? If not: use clean-workspace (whole, resize-only, frame outside) and put the labels in a separate layer whose leaders stop at the image edge (buildable on request), or arrange a native capture.

The callout 'Project Explorer' is later-version (VB6-documented) terminology. VB4's window is titled with the project name ('Loan'), and a VB 4.0-only Microsoft KB article (Q140350) calls it the 'Project window'. The render keeps the ticket copy 'Project Explorer' as instructed. Note that War/SCRIPT.md:133 was already changed to 'Project Window' in commit 9e6f14a (Writing Lead batch) while the ticket/manifest copy still says 'Project Explorer', so the picture and the working script now disagree. Confirm 'Project Window' (the label then needs a producer-approved copy override in src/build.py and a re-render; one label only) or keep 'Project Explorer'? Lower priority: 'Form Designer' is also VB6 documentation wording for what VB4 material calls the form; keep it, or use e.g. 'Form'?

The narration over this visual (War/SCRIPT.md:135) says the form was 'in the center' as 'a blank gray window' and the code window was 'behind all of it'. In the only accepted VB4 capture the form is centre-left, it is a populated sample (LoanSheet), and the Code window is open in front of the form. Toolbox-left and properties-right match. Keep the narration as a general description of the IDE (possibly with 'behind' read as 'the code behind the form'), soften it (for example 'and a code window where you wrote your actual BASIC'), or ask the edit to hold on clean-workspace during that sentence? No script edit was made.

No credit is burned into either variant, because HIST-02's proposed credit ('... Used with permission from Microsoft.') must not be used before the rights basis is decided. If Microsoft's screenshot permission is the chosen basis, where should the required statement go: video description, end credits, or on screen? At 1.5x there is no room inside the text safe area below the screenshot; an on-screen line would need the image reduced slightly (about 1.44x) and a re-render.

Both variants show the 'Loan' project (LOAN.FRM, including its form graphic) whole; its authorship is unestablished and Microsoft's terms exclude screenshots containing third-party content. Inherited unchanged from HIST-02; release of XTRA-05 follows that decision.

The cue says 'Side-by-side — the VB4 IDE with labeled callouts'. Two full-frame stills share an identical screenshot rectangle, so the edit can cut or dissolve from clean-workspace to five-callouts. A literal side-by-side of both would halve the screenshot (about 0.75x) and make its UI text unreadable at 720p. Is cut/dissolve acceptable, or is a split-screen wanted?
